finding.claim: POST /profile/avatar fetches an attacker-supplied URL with axios, which follows redirects by default. The only check is that the first URL starts with https://, so an attacker-controlled https host can 302 to internal http targets (e.g. 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254) that the scheme check never sees. The response length and success/failure are returned to the caller, giving a limited blind SSRF oracle.

trace.note: url = req.body.avatarUrl taken unmodified from the request body
only checks typeof string and url.startsWith("https://"); no host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP block
axios.get called with the raw attacker string; maxRedirects not set to 0 and no beforeRedirect re-validation, so redirects are followed to arbitrary hosts
bytes: img.data.length returned to caller, a length oracle on the fetched body; axios throws on non-2xx, leaking success/failure

finding.guards_checked: Type check on string (line 11) does not constrain destination. startsWith('https://') (line 11) constrains only the first hop's scheme, not host or redirect targets. No host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP block, or DNS pinning anywhere on the path. Redirect following not disabled (no maxRedirects:0, no beforeRedirect hook). Decoy checked: GET /users/:id at server.js:18-21 is NOT a finding: encodeURIComponent (line 19) blocks path/query injection and the host is fixed by the USER_SVC constant (line 7); only '..' path normalization within /v1/ on the same host remains, which is not SSRF.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the type and https:// prefix at server.js:11, which constrains the first hop's scheme and not its host. No host allowlist, private-IP block, or maxRedirects/beforeRedirect control exists anywhere on the path, and axios.get at server.js:14 uses default redirect following.
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10) is unauthenticated and reaches axios.get at server.js:14 after only a startsWith("https://") check (server.js:11), so an https host can 302 to http://127.0.0.1 or 169.254.169.254, and the byte length or error status returned at server.js:15 forms a blind SSRF oracle.
